Master of Social Work Overview

Turn Your Passion for People into a Profession

Social workers are agents of change, equipped with emotional intelligence, clinical expertise, communication, and a deep commitment to empowering individuals, families, groups, and communities. An MSW is one of the more versatile mental health degrees you can earn, leading to a variety of career paths and professional environments to fit your specific goals. 

In the CSWE-accredited, online Master of Social Work (MSW) at Alliant’s California School of Professional Psychology (CSPP), you’ll build the clinical knowledge and practical skills to launch a rewarding and meaningful social service career using innovative deliveries and technologies. You’ll also gain necessary assessment, diagnosis and treatment planning skills and learn how social policy shapes the profession and how you can help play a role in this process.

No matter your undergraduate background, you’re welcome here:

  • If you earned your Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) degree from a CSWE-accredited program, you may qualify for our one-year, online Advanced Standing Master of Social Work program.
  • If your bachelor’s is in any other field, stay on this page to explore our traditional, two-year MSW program.

Whichever track you choose, you’ll graduate practice-ready and confident in your professional identity, Aligned with the Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) pathway, Alliant’s MSW program is designed around advanced clinical practice, preparing you to excel in the field and earn a credential that is widely recognized and respected.

Program Highlights

Flexible. Rigorous. Career-Ready.

CSWE-Accredited Excellence

Our online, CSWE-accredited MSW program is designed to equip you with the clinical skills, policy knowledge, and advocacy tools needed to make a meaningful impact in your community and beyond.

Finish in 12 to 24 months

Choose from full-time, and Advanced Standing pathways with formats designed to fit your life—not disrupt it. You can earn your MSW in as little as two years in the traditional program, or in just one year through our Advanced Standing track.

Gain Experience in Flexible Field Placements

Hands-on experience is at the heart of of clinical practice. We’ll help you find a placement that fits your schedule, even if it involves non-traditional hours. You have the power to choose the internship specialization that works best for you.

Training for Diverse Careers

From micro-level direct practice to macro-level policy and advocacy, our curriculum prepares you for a wide range of roles in your field. You’ll build the knowledge, skills, and experience to pursue the career you’ve envisioned. Graduates may work in schools, child welfare, public health agencies, private practice, substance abuse facilities, hospitals, clinics, and more.

Grounded in Cultural Competency and Community Outreach

MSW students learn to apply principles of cultural competency, cultural humility, and inclusive awareness to help reduce inequities and disparities. You’ll be trained to engage community members and partners to identify community needs, develop interventions and strategies for change, and promote community health and wellness.

Admissions and Financial Aid Info

You’ll be assigned a dedicated admissions counselor to guide you at every step. They’ll keep you on track with application deadlines and requirements, and upon acceptance, work with you and Alliant’s Student Finance Office to explore grants, scholarships, and other financial aid options. Plus, we can help with an unofficial transcript review. We’re your partners and your foundation of support from day one.

  • Hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university
  • Meet the university minimum cumulative GPA requirement for graduate study (3.0 on a 4.0 scale).*
  • Submit official transcripts from all postsecondary institutions attended.
  • Submit a completed graduate application and required university admissions documentation.

*An interview will be required for applicants with a GPA lower than 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.

  • Hold a Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) degree from a CSWE-accredited program, conferred within the last seven years.
  • Meet the university minimum cumulative GPA requirement for graduate study (3.0 on a 4.0 scale).*
  • Submit official transcripts from all postsecondary institutions attended.
  • Submit a completed graduate application and required university admissions documentation.

*An interview will be required for applicants with a GPA lower than 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.

Alliant is committed to making your education accessible and affordable. Financing is available in the form of scholarships, grants, part-time employment, and loans funded through federal, state, Alliant, and private sources. Your Alliant admissions counselor can provide further guidance and information of the specific costs of this program.

New MSW students may qualify for the Social Work Opportunity Grant, a one-time $1,250 tuition award. Learn more about grants and scholarships.

Faculty

Led by Dr. Megan Hampton, the MSW program faculty are experienced clinicians, scholars, and industry leaders actively engaged in social work practice. Faculty integrate real-world clinical experience, current evidence-based practices, and contemporary case applications into every course while remaining deeply committed to supporting students throughout their academic journey and professional careers long after graduation.

Faculty

Frequently Asked Questions

Students pursuing an MSW gain a multicultural and diverse perspective on social work and experience hands-on programs with individual, family, and community exposure. You’ll gain comprehensive skills to tackle the struggles encountered by your clients and a field education internship to gain practical insights and enhance your abilities. You’ll build the clinical skills, practicum experience, and professional identity to become a licensed clinical social worker who can implement effective solutions for your clients. Check out our blog post for more information.

Alliant’s CSWE accreditation ensures that our online MSW program meets specific quality standards and prepares you for licensed practice.

Students who successfully complete the degree requirements for this program will be eligible to apply for licensure through the Association of Social Work Boards (ASWB). Candidates typically take the ASWB Masters exam for intermediate licensure (LMSW) or the ASWB Clinical exam for clinical licensure (LCSW). Please note that licensure requirements vary from state to state, so students should refer to this page and contact the licensing board in the state they wish to apply for licensure.

The program is offered in 15-week trimester sessions. You can find a copy of our academic calendar here.

The MSW program is offered fully online in an asynchronous format with no required set meeting times and is designed with a strong clinical focus, including integrated licensure exam preparation throughout the curriculum. Our work-life balance approach is designed for working adults with flexibility, prioritizing student learning while accommodating personal obligations.

Program Learning Outcomes and Goals

  1. Demonstrate Ethical and Professional Behavior
  2. Advance Human Rights and Social, Racial, Economic, and Environmental Justice
  3. Engage Anti-Racism, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (ADEI) in Practice
  4. Engage in Practice-Informed Research and Research-Informed Practice
  5. Engage in Policy Practice
  6. Engage with Individuals, Families, Groups, Organizations, and Communities
  7. Assess Individuals, Families, Groups, Organizations, and Communities
  8. Intervene with Individuals, Families, Groups, Organizations, and Communities
  9. Evaluate Practice with Individuals, Families, Groups, Organizations, and Communities
Assessment outcomes Form AS 4 (M)

Where Passion Meets Purpose

CSPP’s Social Work Matters podcast, hosted by Dr. Megan Hampton, LISW, LCSW, director of Alliant’s MSW program, is the space to learn about every aspect of being a social worker, social work education, professional development, and why we need highly qualified social workers today more than ever.
